title: the librarian's hash-keyed memory moves onto reserved rows of the four Q#108 tables, dropping nothing
intention: One idempotent migration (dry run by default, --write applies) lays every hash-keyed librarian node in cairn_nodes as a DATA row reserved through trees.reserve() in cairn_mem_nodes. meta carries provenance and standing verbatim plus the old hash as legacy_id, and no confidence key. Embeddings and links follow onto the addresses. Every standing leaf table, vector or keyed, gains an additive row bigint column filled 1..n, its node_id rewritten to the node's address with the old hash kept in an additive legacy_node_id column, its tag drawn from the registry, and the node's in list holding the leaf back. No old row is dropped.
why: Measured 2026-11-14: T2 (06db586bedfd) moves the trees tool onto the Q#108 schema (outline 4.3.1.5.1.6), but the live memory is still hash-keyed. cairn_nodes holds 46107 rows (44582 hypothesis, 802 refuted, 723 earned), cairn_embeddings 28496, cairn_links 7, and 17 standing leaf tables plus the keyed inferenceproxy_answers_nodes (16246 rows) carry text hash node_ids and no row column. So once the 06db group lands, T2's code reads none of it, and 2b3d842bc118's clause 6 already reds today on 'SELECT max(row) FROM inferenceproxy_answers_nodes' (UndefinedColumn). The seed's migrate_to_row_ids.py was cut from T2 (its D4) because it targeted the seed's cairn_node_rows, not the four tables.
traces_to: Law 1 (the settled memory is carried, not re-derived), Law 6 (each leaf is written through its owner's gate under its recorded owner), Law 7 (a node or leaf that cannot be mapped is named in the report, never silently dropped); outline 4.3.1.5.1.6 and 4.3.1.5.1.6.11.
how: Re-shape the seed's migrate_to_row_ids.py onto the four tables. It runs inside the trees tool, so it uses the tool's own doors (reserve, write_node, _hold_content, leaf_tag, link, the list append). It writes tenant leaf tables only through store's owner-gated doors (add_owned_column from the add-column branch eaf98e8ab, add_owned_index(unique=True) from the add-unique-index branch 891004b36, update) under store.owner_of(table). The legacy table names are injectable, so the proof runs it over store.scratch tables in the legacy shapes.

outcomes.claim: every legacy node lands as exactly one DATA row in cairn_mem_nodes at a row handed out by trees.reserve(), kind text, its content as payload (or a blob past INLINE_MAX), meta.provenance and meta.standing equal to the legacy row's provenance and standing, and meta.legacy_id the old hash

confidence is ABSENT: no migrated node's meta has a confidence key, including a legacy node whose provenance carries one (that value stays verbatim inside meta.provenance), and trees.read_node of a migrated node reads unscored

THE ROW CLAUSE: after --write every standing leaf table, vector and keyed, has a row bigint column whose values are 1..n with no gaps, no nulls and no duplicates, held by a UNIQUE index laid through store.add_owned_index(unique=True) so a second row with the same value is refused; 'SELECT max(row) FROM <keyed leaf>' returns n; each leaf's node_id is the node's address as digits, its old hash is in legacy_node_id, its table tag came from the tag registry at 0x0100 or above, and the node's in list holds that leaf's address; each leaf's leaf_id is rewritten to trees.leaf_id_for(address, new eid), or leaf_id_for(address, key) for a keyed leaf, the old one kept in an additive legacy_leaf_id column

embeddings and links follow: each legacy embedding whose node maps lands in cairn_mem_embeddings with embedding_id = trees.embedding_id_for(address, render_method) and the node's address (the legacy row stays untouched in cairn_embeddings, its old id readable there); each legacy link lands as one link row through trees.link with its weight and traversals kept; and re-depositing already-migrated content after --write moves neither the embedding count nor the leaf count

nothing is dropped: the legacy nodes, embeddings and links tables keep their row counts and contents through --write; a leaf table keeps its row count; an embedding, link or leaf whose hash maps to no node is named by id in the report and left untouched
content already held at an address (a deposit made after T2 landed) maps the legacy hash onto that address and appends the legacy provenance as an attestation; no second node row is laid
the dry run writes nothing (every new and legacy table's row count is unchanged), and a second --write lays no row, column, index or tag

outcomes.text: migrate_to_row_ids.py, re-shaped from the seed (94da6412d) onto cairn_mem_nodes/lists/links/blobs, cairn_mem_embeddings, cairn_mem_content_index and cairn_mem_tags. Order: nodes (reserve, write_node, content index, meta.legacy_id), then embeddings, links and leaves (add_owned_column row and legacy_node_id, fill row 1..n in leaf_id order, then add_owned_index(<leaf>, owner, '<leaf>_row_key', ['row'], unique=True), copy the hash, rewrite node_id, leaf_tag, append the leaf address to the node's in list). Scratch-shaped leaf tables are skipped: they are not standing, and ensure_trees refuses them since 1a3a55a314eb. The report is JSON (counts before and after, laid, mapped onto held content, unmapped ids per table). It exits 1 when a legacy table's count moved during the run or a mapped node did not land. --legacy takes a JSON map of table names, for the proof. Ids follow the address: a migrated embedding's id is trees.embedding_id_for(address, render_method) and a leaf's leaf_id is trees.leaf_id_for(address, eid|key), the old leaf id kept in an additive legacy_leaf_id column, so deposit's lid dedupe recognises migrated content.

the red-first proof, one tooth per clause, test_-named, over store.scratch tables only: scratch legacy nodes/embeddings/links tables in the legacy shapes (including a node whose provenance carries confidence, an orphan embedding and a leaf naming an unknown hash), one scratch vector leaf and one scratch keyed leaf. Clause 3's tooth inserts a duplicate row after --write and asserts the refusal. Clause 6 deposits through trees.deposit first. Red before D1 (the module is absent).
